context.objective: Document how we carry out Due to Manager: Expense Transfer, the controls and what needs confirmation.

turns.text: Thanks for sharing. Give me a moment to digest the file. Then I’ll follow up with a question.

The procedure describes reconciling source, prepared, and fund-system totals and retaining a reviewer’s record, but leaves the allowed difference and reviewer role unspecified. Does that description reflect how this work is carried out today?

Yes, that matches what we do. After the data is recorded in the fund system, the preparer and the reviewer confirm that the source totals, the prepared totals and the totals recorded in the fund system all agree, check that vendor and category records match, and investigate any combined or rejected lines. All exceptions get resolved and we keep the reviewer sign-off or review record. The rule is that no unexplained difference can remain in the totals or the set of records. If they do not reconcile, we resolve the difference before anything goes to billing, and the GPFS reviewer or the client decides as needed. I do not know of any allowed difference amount, and the exact reviewer role is not defined, so I cannot tell you either of those.
What typically prompts the management company to send the expense set for this transfer?

It starts when the management company has bills or expenses to allocate to the funds and gives the fund team an organized expense file. The timing depends on the client. In the US reimbursement model the management company pays the expenses and bills the funds quarterly, but the schedule has to be confirmed for each client, so I cannot give you one fixed calendar. Before we start we confirm the export is complete, the expense categories and client mapping are available, vendor names and codes match the target system or have documented exceptions, the required approvals and supporting documents are available, and the preparer has access to the target fund system.
What does completing this transfer enable for the funds or the management company?

It gets the expenses the management company paid into the fund accounting records so the correct funds record or reimburse the amounts they owe to the manager. The process ends when the approved due-to-manager data set is recorded in the fund accounting system and the reviewed package is sent on to the client billing or invoicing process, where the funds or portfolio companies get billed later. Before that handoff the reviewer confirms the items and totals sent to billing match the reviewed data set, and we keep the completion communication and record where the package is stored. One more rule: if any row, mapping or total changes during preparation or review, we repeat the full check from the source data through preparation and fund-system entry and get the final version approved again. The standard approval sequence and the package storage location are not defined, so I do not know those.
What can go wrong for the funds or management company if this transfer or billing handoff is delayed or incorrect?

memo_findings.answer: The supplied process name is Due to Manager: Expense Transfer; the procedure abbreviates it DTM and identifies it as MC-02.

The documented work records and reviews management-company expense data in the fund system and passes an approved package to billing.
The transfer puts management-company-paid expenses into fund accounting records so the correct funds record or reimburse amounts owed to the manager.

The work starts when the management company has bills or expenses to allocate to funds and gives the fund team an organized expense file. Timing depends on the client.
In the US reimbursement model, the management company pays expenses and bills the funds quarterly; the schedule must be confirmed for each client rather than assumed to be a fixed calendar.
The applicable schedule and any fixed deadlines must be confirmed for each client.

The procedure's completion output is a complete DTM package and confirmation that the next process accepted it; totals sent to billing must match the reviewed data set.
The participant says the process ends when the approved due-to-manager data set is recorded in the fund accounting system and the reviewed package is sent to client billing or invoicing; funds or portfolio companies are billed later.
The procedure requires confirmation of next-process acceptance, while the participant identifies sending the package as the finish; whether acceptance is part of actual completion needs clarification.
The roles table says the process owner and internal approver are not yet confirmed.

The roles table assigns the management-company accounting preparer responsibility for recording expenses, assigning source categories and producing the export.
The procedure directs the GPFS fund-team preparer to log the source system, period, entities and file version, check expected expenses and categories, and compare source totals to the management-company control total. Missing control totals or unclear records are referred to the management company.
The documented GPFS preparer and reviewer check categories against approved fund categories, identify missing or inconsistently coded vendors, resolve unmatched or duplicate vendors through the approved vendor-record process, and confirm the mapping version and applicable period.
The preparer confirms the client-validated entry method, target system and access, with confirmation from the client or process owner. The preparer applies approved mappings and preserves vendor detail where supported; manual entries retain source links, while an approved upload uses a validated template and required client-dependent checks. Results and rejected items are recorded.
The preparer and reviewer reconcile source, prepared and fund-system totals and vendor and category records, investigate combined or rejected lines, and resolve exceptions. Where approved system design supports it, they confirm whether amounts are owed to the manager or an affiliate.
The documented preparer and reviewer, with client-specific roles, assemble the approved data, mapping, reconciliation, support and review record; send the approved items to billing or the client's invoicing or distribution process; and retain the completion communication and package location.
Client-specific schedules and practical implementation of the documented preparation and entry steps remain to be confirmed.
The participant confirms that after recording in the fund system, the preparer and reviewer compare source, prepared and recorded totals, check vendor and category records, investigate combined or rejected lines and resolve exceptions. Differences are resolved before anything goes to billing, with the GPFS reviewer or client deciding as needed.
Before starting, the team confirms export completeness, availability of expense categories and client mapping, matching vendor names and codes or documented exceptions, required approvals and supporting documents, and preparer access to the target fund system.
If any row, mapping or total changes during preparation or review, the team repeats the full check from source data through preparation and fund-system entry and obtains approval again for the final version.

The procedure requires documentation of intake period, entities and totals before preparation; unapproved vendor or category mappings must not be applied. Rejected lines must appear in the exception log, and recorded rows and totals must match approved prepared data.
The procedure requires no unexplained difference in totals or records and retention of reviewer sign-off or a review record. For an unapproved mapping mismatch, it directs the team to stop the affected item until resolution is documented.
The exact reviewer role, allowed difference, new-vendor approval process and standard package approval sequence are not specified or confirmed in the procedure.
The participant confirms the preparer and reviewer reconcile the three sets of totals and vendor and category records, investigate combined or rejected lines, resolve exceptions and retain reviewer sign-off or a review record. No unexplained difference may remain in totals or records.
The participant does not know of a numerical allowed difference and says the exact reviewer role is not defined.
The participant reports pre-start checks for a complete export, available categories and mapping, matched vendor names and codes or documented exceptions, required approvals and support, and preparer system access.
Before handoff, the reviewer confirms that the items and totals sent to billing match the reviewed data set.
When a row, mapping or total changes during preparation or review, the full source-to-entry check is repeated and the final version is approved again.

The procedure describes client-validated manual entry, upload or another approved method; upload checks depend on the client. It says the One Rock method cannot be assumed for another client.
Timing varies by client. The participant describes quarterly fund billing in the US reimbursement model, but says each client's schedule must be confirmed.

The documented working artifacts include the management-company export and support, intake checklist, client mapping, vendor and mapping exception log, upload template, DTM reconciliation, fund-system report and review record.
The supplied procedure distinguishes supporting operating instructions, which require current-owner approval, from client and design files that show examples or proposed design and do not establish current general requirements without approval.
The management company supplies an organized expense file to the fund team. The participant also identifies client mapping, documented vendor exceptions, approvals and supporting documents as intake readiness materials.
The team retains the completion communication and records where the reviewed package is stored.
The participant says the package storage location is not defined.

The procedure describes a GPFS fund-team process using management-company expense data, with client-specific mapping and entry methods, and labels its baseline current documented GPFS practice. The participant confirmed the reconciliation and review description, not the entire procedure.

The procedure says the client-approved method sets category and vendor mapping, allocations, included records, support, entry method and target fields. A detailed client-specific procedure, when applicable, requires completion and a completion record before proceeding.
The participant states that no unexplained difference can remain in totals or records, and a reconciliation difference must be resolved before billing.
Before work starts, vendor names and codes must match the target system or have documented exceptions; required approvals and supporting documents must be available.
A change to any row, mapping or total during preparation or review requires a full source-to-fund-system recheck and renewed final-version approval.

The process consumes the management-company accounting preparer's expense export and sends an approved package to billing or the client's invoicing or distribution process. The procedure requires confirmation of acceptance by the next process.
Uses the output of Management-company accounting expense preparation: Expense export and supporting data for the period.
Hands off to Billing or client invoicing or distribution process: Approved package after review; next-process acceptance is required.
The participant confirms that reconciliation differences are resolved before anything goes to billing.
Hands off to Billing or client invoicing or distribution process: Approved package after review; reconciliation differences must be resolved before billing, and the procedure requires next-process acceptance.
Uses the output of Management-company accounting expense preparation: The management company supplies the fund team an organized expense file when it has bills or expenses to allocate to funds.
The participant says the reviewed package is sent to client billing or invoicing after recording; the reviewer checks that its items and totals match the reviewed data set.
Hands off to Billing or client invoicing or distribution process: The reviewed package is sent after fund-system recording; differences are resolved and the reviewer checks items and totals. The procedure also requires next-process acceptance.

The procedure lists an Excel export and describes manual entry in Allvue or Entrilia or a validated upload. It cautions that the actual target system must be confirmed and Intralinks should not be assumed to be it.
